card.name: Meke
card.tagline: Fiji's umbrella tradition of narrative song-and-dance
card.profile: Meke is the Fijian term for the traditional complex of song and dance, a cognate of Tongan 'me'e' and Samoan 'me' (Wikipedia). Performed at celebrations and festivals, it serves as a living oral archive encoding legends, genealogies and historical events. A performance has two groups: the vakatara (orchestra of singers and instrumentalists using derua bamboo tubes and lali wooden gongs) and the matana (dancers). Dances were traditionally taught by daunivucu, who in tradition received them from the spirit world. Sub-forms include the meke wesi (spear dance), meke i wau (club dance), seasea (women's fan dance), vakamalolo (seated dance) and taralala (Wikipedia; Fiji Times).
card.insight: Meke is central to iTaukei identity because pre-literate Fijian society used it to transmit history and law; German ethnographer Friedrich Ratzel documented it as combined song-and-dance in his 1896 'The History of Mankind' (Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: Fijian dance-and-chant of legend. A representative image shows grass or tapa attire and synchronized group motion in an open-air island setting — Fiji, Fiji.
